bug_semantics: load_checkpoint_in_model (and load_checkpoint_and_dispatch, which calls it) reads a sharded checkpoint *.index.json, takes untrusted weight_map values, and joins them onto the checkpoint directory with os.path.join and no sanitization. Relative ../ segments escape the directory; an absolute shard name discards the folder prefix. Those paths are then opened by load_state_dict (safetensors.safe_open for .safetensors, else torch.load(..., weights_only=True)). A malicious checkpoint can open files outside the folder as an existence/parse oracle, or point a shard at a FIFO so the torch.load branch blocks indefinitely. Not RCE: safetensors uses safe_open and the torch branch already passes weights_only=True.

potential_fix.approach: Validate each sharded-checkpoint weight_map value before join: reject empty/non-string and absolute names, normalize the joined path without realpath, and raise ValueError unless it stays inside checkpoint_folder. Optionally reject non-regular shard files so torch.load cannot block on FIFOs.
potential_fix.rationale: os.path.join follows .. segments and discards the checkpoint folder when the shard name is absolute, so load_state_dict opens attacker-chosen paths. A string-normalized containment check closes CWE-22 without breaking Hugging Face hub-cache symlink layouts; a regular-file check closes the named-pipe hang.
